messages.author: 08a38a1b55af9c04
messages.subject: multinomPois when M=1?
parts:
Hello All,

Can multinomPois be used to fit a removal model when sampling does not occur in spatially distinct subpopulations?  For example, can the lobster removal analysis in Pollock et al. (1984) (Biometrics 40, 329-340) using effort and temperature covariates be conducted using multnomPois?  I assume this is a situation where M=1; the covariates would be observation level, indexed only on J (# of removals).

Thanks,
Steve Hayes

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] multinomPois when M=1?
parts:
hi Steve,
in principle, this should work, but the function in unmarked might not be
set up to handle that situation because the data structure being a special
case.
In general, with M=1, I'm guessing there are important limitations on the
types of covariate models you can fit (i.e., that are identifiable), so be
careful.
regards
andy
